name: Application Layer
description: Models the application architecture: application components (deployable modules, classes and services), the application functions and processes that describe their internal behaviour, the application services and interfaces through which that behaviour is exposed, application events and interactions, collaborations between components, and the data objects they process (ArchiMate 3.2 application layer). This is the default home for ordinary application code structure; more specific layers apply only when a symbol is itself an API contract, a data schema, a persistence object, a UI element, telemetry, security logic or a test asset. Modelling rules: components and collaborations are assigned to the functions, processes and interactions they perform (assigned-to), and a collaboration aggregates its components and nested collaborations. A component provides the interfaces its own code declares and is assigned to an interface it only handles; an interface is assigned to the services it offers. Functions, processes and interactions realize application services; a component may realize one directly, as a shortcut through the behaviour assigned to it. Services serve the components, functions, processes and interactions that use them. Functions, processes, interactions, events and services access data objects, and so do components, unlike in the business layer, because a component is code that holds and passes data; interfaces and collaborations do not. Events trigger processes, interactions and functions (unlike a business function, an application function can be an event handler), and behaviour raises events. A hand-off between behaviours is flows-to; depends-on means one element needs another to work, and is never used where assigned-to, accesses, serves or triggers says it. Across layers, application processes and functions realize the business processes and functions they automate, and application services realize business services and product features and capabilities and, with the behaviour that realizes them, carry the link to motivation (realize goals, satisfy requirements and constraints, deliver value).
